title: Potential-force commutator obstruction for the resolvent-smoothed coordinate
question: Does the potential-force term V'(q) f'(q) in the second Heisenberg commutator remain uniformly K-form bounded for the fixed resolvent-smoothed coordinate f(q)=16q/(16+q^2)?

model.localization_consequence: On translated compactly supported C1 bumps with bounded derivative energy C_phi, the numerator potential contribution grows like R^6 while the denominator K-form grows like R^4; the ratio is therefore unbounded in this K-form route.

adversarial_review.check: The lower bounds use absolute values for the force and resolvent derivative on y>=64; no sign cancellation is assumed.
The shifted quartic potential is lower-bounded by y^2/20 on the declared region; the positive shift is retained rather than dropped with an incorrect sign.
The unbounded ratio is stated for translated compact-support C1 bumps with an explicit finite derivative-energy symbol C_phi; no Gaussian normalization or hidden boundary limit is used.
Only the V'f' potential part of a second commutator is obstructed; kinetic f'', f''' and f'''' terms and cancellation-aware combinations remain open.
The result rejects the naive K-form multiplication route, not all higher-energy, state-weighted or modular estimates.
No common-alpha nonexistence, OS/KMS/GNS result, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion follows.
